title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Reference Architectures, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended guidance for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers: reference architectures, packaging and distribution options, pre-deployment customer requirements, day-2 operational practices, and safe upgrade & rollback procedures. Intended audience: solutions engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and customer ops teams.

Scope

- Valid for Private control plane deployments (Redwood-managed control plane + customer VPC) and fully on-prem (air-gapped) bundles.
- Covers supported deployment topologies, packaging options (OCI/Tarball/VM image), day-2 operational runbooks, and standardized upgrade/rollback playbooks.
- Excludes CI build internals and low-level kernel tuning; those are in eng-serving-runtime docs.

Quick summary of recommendations

1. Use the VPC deployment template for cloud-connected private deployments; use the on-prem installer for air-gapped customers.
2. Always run a canary upgrade before fleet-wide rollout (5% of machines, representative traffic).
3. Configure Prometheus + Loki + Tempo for observability and integrate exportable audit logs to customer SIEM/KMS.

Prerequisites (customer-facing checklist)

- Network: CIDR ranges, peering/VPN details, allowed outbound hosts (control-plane endpoints), firewall rules for NTP/HTTPS (443).
- Identity & Keys: KMS/HSM endpoint, service account with least privilege, optional SAML/OIDC for console.
- Storage: NFS or S3-compatible object store for model artifacts and backups.
- Compute: Inventory of GPU and CPU nodes, driver versions (NVIDIA driver >= 525.xx for Ampere/T4), container runtime (containerd 1.6+ recommended).
- Audit & Compliance: Destination for audit logs and retention window.

Reference architectures

1) VPC-connected private deployment (Recommended for most enterprise customers)

- Components: customer VPC (subnets: control, compute, ops), Redwood control-plane endpoints (regional), NAT/peering, optional private-link.
- Typical sizing (example table):

| Workload | Nodes | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Control plane (regional HA) | 3 | m5.large equivalents; not GPU-bound |
| Serving GPU pool | 2-10 per model tier | 1-8 GPUs per node depending on chassis |
| Batch/Preprocessing | 0-4 | CPU-only nodes for preprocessing and evals |
| Observability & Logging | 2 | Prometheus + Grafana + Loki replicas |

- Network: minimal egress to control-endpoints (443), NTP (123), and monitoring endpoints. Use security groups to restrict API access.

2) On-prem / air-gapped deployment (Regulated environments)

- Components packaged as offline OCI tarball + installer. All images must be scanned and signed; provide image signing metadata.
- Hardware: nodes behind customer firewall; expect isolated DNS and no external connectivity.

Packaging & distribution options

- Cloud-connected (VPC) installer: Helm charts + Terraform module for bootstrapping VPC components. Delivered as public OCI images.
- On-prem offline bundle: signed tarball containing: manifests/, images.tar.gz, installer binary, license blob, notarization metadata.
- VM image option: OVA/AMI for customers who prefer non-containerized deployments.

On-prem bundle example layout:

/redwood-bundle-2026.3.0/
  - images.tar.gz
  - manifests/
  - installer (linux)
  - checksums.txt
  - license.json
  - signing/ (signature.pub, signature.sig)

Packaging validation steps (deliverable to customer)

1. Checksum validation: sha256sum -c checksums.txt
2. Verify signatures: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify signature.pub -signature signature.sig images.tar.gz
3. Validate manifests: redwood-installer validate manifests/ --level=strict

Day-2 operations (operational playbook)

Operational goals: maintain availability (99.95% cluster uptime), predictable latency (P95 serving latency targets per model), and cost visibility.

Monitoring & alerting

- Metrics: request_rate, token_rate, latency_p50/p95, gpu_utilization, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_load_time.
- Recommended alert thresholds:
  - GPU utilization > 90% for 10m -> scale up or add capacity (alert: high-gpu-utilization)
  - P95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 5m -> investigate slowdowns (alert: latency-regression)
  - Model load failures > 1/min -> rollback canary and alert (alert: model-load-fail)
  - Disk usage > 85% -> run cleanup or expand PVC (alert: disk-near-capacity)

Prometheus alert example:

- alert: HighGPUUtilization
  expr: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization[10m]) > 90
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU utilization > 90% on {{ $labels.instance }}"

Logging & traces

- Forward application logs to Loki; use structured JSON. Ensure request_id and trace_id are present in all logs.
- Trace sampling: 5% distributed traces in steady state, 100% for canary/upgrade windows.

Backups & model artifact management

- Models and checkpoints stored in S3-compatible store. Daily incremental backups, weekly full backups. Retention policy configured per customer (default 30 days).
- Validate model artifact checksum before deployment.

Routine operational procedures (day-2 checklists)

1. Daily morning check (SRE oncall):
   - Verify control plane health: redwoodctl cluster status
   - Check Prometheus target scraping (no targets down)
   - Inspect error budget burn rate dashboard
2. Weekly maintenance:
   - Rotate TLS certs if expiring within 30 days
   - Apply minor security patches during maintenance window
3. Monthly capacity review:
   - Review model usage, tail latency, and recommend scaling or batching changes

Upgrade & rollback procedures (safe rollout pattern)

Principles:
- Upgrades are staged: canary -> phased cohort rollout -> full rollout. Always have a tested rollback plan.
- Maintain immutable model & runtime image tags for reproducibility.

Pre-upgrade steps (run by release lead)

1. Read release notes and breaking-change matrix.
2. Verify canary test plan: traffic profile, smoke tests, and regression evals.
3. Take consistent backups of model artifacts and backup control plane DB (timestamped).
4. Notify stakeholders and schedule maintenance window.

Canary upgrade (example steps)

1. Deploy new release to canary subset (5% of serving nodes) using Helm with override: helm upgrade --install redwood --set replicaCountCanary=2 ./chart --namespace redwood
2. Route traffic: update routing policy to send 5% production traffic to canary nodes (redwood-routingctl set-canary --percent 5)
3. Run smoke tests and evaluation prompts (see smoke-tests.yaml).
4. Monitor for 30-60 minutes for: error rate increase > 1.5x baseline, latency regressions, model-quality regressions (predefined eval set).
5. If OK, proceed to phased rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%).

Rollback procedure (if canary fails or regression detected)

1. Immediately remove canary from traffic: redwood-routingctl set-canary --percent 0
2. Rollback Helm release to previous revision: helm rollback redwood <REVISION>
3. Revert any infra changes (Terraform apply -var=previous=true).
4. Open incident and tag as upgrade-regression; attach logs and eval runs.
5. Schedule postmortem and block further rollouts until mitigation.

Rollback example commands:

redwoodctl cluster drain --selector=canary=true
helm rollback redwood 42
redwoodctl config validate

Validation & post-upgrade checks

- Confirm cluster health: redwoodctl cluster status -> all components green
- Run regression evals and compare against baseline (accuracy, hallucination rate)
- Confirm SLO telemetry is within expected variance for 24h

Customer requirements library (mapping to configuration)

| Customer requirement | Minimum config / artifact | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Air-gapped install | On-prem bundle + offline installer | eng-private-deployments|
| HSM-backed keys | KMS/HSM connector config (pkcs11) | security-and-compliance|
| Audit retention 7 years | Audit export pipeline + retention policy | security-and-compliance|
| FIPS-140-2 runtime | FIPS-enabled OS image + validated runtime | eng-infra|

Operational roles & ownership

- Deployment owner: Solutions Engineering (requester & approver for initial deployment).
- Day-2 oncall: Eng-SRE (primary) and Eng-Platform (secondary).
- Upgrade lead: Release Engineer (coordinates canary and phased rollout).

Troubleshooting common failure modes

- Failed model load: check model artifact checksum, S3 permissions, and model-server logs (error: failed to mmap). Re-upload artifact and reload model-router.
- High GPU OOMs: reduce batch size, enable dynamic batching limits, or deploy more nodes.
- Control plane auth failures: validate service account token TTL and clock drift (ntpcheck).

Example verification commands

- Cluster status: redwoodctl cluster status --output=json
- Check model health: redwoodctl model status --model my-model --verbose
- Fetch logs (last 1h): redwoodctl logs --selector=component=model-server --since=1h | jq '.'

Appendices

A. Network port matrix

| Port | Protocol | Purpose | Direction |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 443 | TLS | Control plane API | outbound/inbound (depends on topology)|
| 123 | NTP | Time sync | outbound|
| 8200 | HTTP | Prometheus metrics | inbound (ops subnet)|
| 9095 | HTTP | Health checks | inbound|

B. Example Terraform snippet (VPC peering):

module "redwood_vpc" {
  source = "redwood/vpc-module/aws"
  cidr_block = "10.10.0.0/16"
  public_subnets = ["10.10.1.0/24"]
  private_subnets = ["10.10.2.0/24"]
}

C. Rollout checklist (pre-flight)

- [ ] Release notes reviewed and signed off
- [ ] Backups completed and verified
- [ ] Canary smoke tests defined and automated
- [ ] Oncall roster notified and pager ready
